trickyParts: Adoption bumps every adopted record's generation: that is the fence the old self-tree's LingerClose, supervise and issue-suspend rows already check; WorkspaceRemove had none, so it now names its tree.
A refused ChildAdoption must write nothing: intake commits a refused fact, so admission checks every child before any write and skips releaseInactiveSlots and promote on a refusal.

The sweep adopts nested queued roots top-down: a candidate whose target is itself a candidate waits for the next pass, so each joins the live tree once, at its top; a parent cycle leaves them as roots.

D2: the ancestor walk runs at preparation, outside the fact lock, and is kept on the record (issues.ancestor_tree), because admission does no Dispatch I/O; record.Waiting evaluates liveness at read time, so a closed tree releases the hold.
Pod lanes: the daemon package's NATS tests ran against a local nats-server via LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL/LEGION_TEST_NATS_MONITOR_URL; Postgres is the embedded zonky build on port 54352.
The hold now stores the recorded ancestor's key, so it follows that ancestor if it is itself a queued root later adopted into the live tree (the stored tree would have gone stale).
An unrecorded ancestor's event creates no record, so admission returns early on it today; the Reread must still reach release and promotion on those early returns.

The shared pod database had the old 0051 applied (version recorded), so the renamed migration never ran there; the column was renamed by hand in that test database only. CI and production start fresh: 0051 was never released.
deviations: Spec departure D1 (accepted by the architect): a root with a tree_lifecycles or handed_over_roots row keeps queueing as its own root, and release_children refuses it CHILD_NOT_ADOPTABLE.

Spec departure D2 is no longer a gap: on the architect's reversal (Envoy 495d1feb672177477e891f5fdec91938) a root under an unrecorded child of a live tree is held out of the line (preparation reads the Dispatch chain; bound: the first recorded ancestor, a missing parent, a repeated key or the issue itself, as release_children's walk has no numeric limit).
Live proof runs admission at cap 2, not 1: a second slotted root lets step 5 free a slot without the live tree leaving.

Simplify skipped two findings: moving the daemon-only AncestorTree off dispatch.IssueSummary (the held pending summaries need it), and an in-memory ancestor walk for the boot listing (few todo issues sit under unrecorded parents).
The reviewer's fast-follow tidy-up was done in this pull request rather than deferred.
The merge with main changed the shared liveDispatch stand-in (404 for an unknown key, parent and label per issue); merged-root-waits.sh and no-required-checks.sh pass on it.
discoveredComplexity: Every todo event of an unrecorded issue or a recorded root under an unrecorded Dispatch parent now costs one Dispatch read per ancestor at preparation, labelled or not.
Every event of an unrecorded issue now reads the issues table once at preparation; Dispatch is read only when a parented queued root exists (normally none).
